skill.name: better-ui
skill.description: Reviews and improves interface polish through precise guidance for surfaces, icons, motion, optical alignment, and interaction feedback.
skill.summary: Apply practical design engineering rules to make existing interfaces more coherent, responsive, and polished.

content.user_title: Polish Interfaces with Precise UI Guidance
content.value_statement: Small inconsistencies in motion, surfaces, and icons can make an interface feel unfinished. This skill provides concrete rules and values for focused improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews nested border radii, optical alignment, surface depth, and image outlines.
Recommends interruptible transitions, restrained motion, staggered entrances, and subtle exits.
Improves icon weight, sizing, state treatment, animation, and right-to-left behavior.
Identifies broad transitions and inappropriate will-change usage that can reduce performance.
Produces severity-ranked findings with locations, suggested changes, rationale, and verification status.
limitations: Focuses on interface polish rather than complete visual redesigns or brand strategy.
Defers accessibility, typography, and layout concerns to separate specialized skills.
Browser-based verification depends on access to a running interface and development tools.
Fixed motion values may require adjustment when an established product system specifies different standards.

use_cases.title: Review a product interface
use_cases.description: Audit an existing interface for inconsistent surfaces, icon treatment, and motion behavior before release.

use_cases.title: Refine frontend components
use_cases.description: Apply exact CSS and component guidance to buttons, cards, image treatments, and animated states.

use_cases.title: Standardize a design system
use_cases.description: Turn repeated interface issues into consistent rules for motion, elevation, icon weight, and state feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Quick interface review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface for visible UI polish issues. List each issue by severity, location, suggested change, and user impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first review of one page or component.

prompt_templates.title: Polish a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this component while preserving its design system. Check radius, alignment, surfaces, icon weight, interaction feedback, and motion values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when refining an existing component implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit motion behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit every animated state in this interface. Check interruptibility, duration, easing, first-render behavior, theme switching, exits, and static feedback cues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for interfaces with several transitions or state changes.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a complete polish audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect all supplied interface files and available browser states. Group root causes, cite every location, propose exact fixes, and report unverified checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before release for a comprehensive, evidence-based review.

output_examples.input: Review a card with equal inner and outer radii and eight pixels of padding.
output_examples.output: MEDIUM: The nested radii are not concentric. Increase the outer radius by eight pixels to match the visible inset.

output_examples.input: Review a toolbar that uses mixed icon libraries and transition-all.
output: MEDIUM: Mixed stroke conventions make toolbar icons visually inconsistent. Use one icon library for the surface.
MEDIUM: The broad transition can animate unintended properties. Name only the properties that change.

output_examples.input: Review a theme toggle that slowly crossfades the whole page.
output_examples.output: HIGH: Theme colors transition together and obscure the state change. Disable transitions during the theme update, then restore them after the next paint.

best_practices: Preserve the project's component library, tokens, density, and established motion language.
Inspect every defined state and report any browser checks that could not be completed.
Group repeated symptoms under one root cause and cite every affected location.
anti_patterns: Do not replace structural borders or accessible focus outlines with decorative shadows.
Do not use transition-all or persistent will-change declarations across many elements.
Do not add expressive motion to frequent interactions or make motion the only state cue.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews surface depth, nested radii, optical alignment, icons, animations, transitions, and interaction feedback.

faq.question: Does it redesign complete products?
faq.answer: No. It improves established interfaces while preserving the existing component system, visual language, and density.

faq.question: Can it work without a browser?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect source-defined states and values, but it must mark visual and runtime behavior as unverified.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Only related polish concerns are covered. Focus behavior, ARIA, hit areas, keyboard support, and reduced motion require an accessibility review.

faq.question: Which motion libraries does it support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for CSS transitions, Motion, and Framer Motion while following the package already used by the project.

faq.question: How are findings reported?
faq.answer: Findings are grouped by principle and ordered by severity, with locations, before and after guidance, rationale, and verification status.
